standards.applies_to: San Diego County only, ddPCR (copies/100 mL) results. Developed by the California Department of Public Health for San Diego County; the San Diego Water Board states it has no water quality objective for ddPCR results. Measured: every copies/100 mL row in the state dataset is San Diego (Region 9), so the threshold's scope and the data's scope coincide.
standards.verbatim: The California Regional Water Quality Control Board – San Diego Region (San Diego Water Board) does not currently have a water-quality objective for Enterococcus ddPCR results. However, the California Department of Public Health developed for San Diego County a standard threshold value of 1,413 copies/100 mL in equivalence with the state culture-based threshold of 104 CFU/100 mL. When samples exceed this standard threshold value of 1,413 copies/100 mL Enterococcus, DEHQ will issue Bacterial Exceedance Advisories under the Beach and Bay Water Quality Monitoring program.
standards.scope_verbatim: Results from the ddPCR analyses are reported as copies/100 mL and are presented separately from traditional culture-based results (which are reported in CFU/100 mL or MPN/100 mL).

scope_rules.finding: A county health officer's beach posting and the state's water quality objectives are two different instruments. Postings run on the title 17 beach notification levels; the objectives in this file are what the state's Safe to Swim map and its published geometric means compare against. The Ocean Plan says so and then says the title 17 standards are not water quality objectives. This app compares against the objectives, because those are the numbers behind the data it holds — so it must never say a beach is posted, closed, or unposted ON ITS OWN AUTHORITY, and must never present its own reading as a posting. NARROWED 2026-09-17 (R35): where a NAMED county publishes its own posting through a public data service this app reads, that county's posting IS shown — in the county's own words, in quotation marks, attributed to the county by name, and carried with the time this app read it. It is never merged into the tier computed here. The two instruments stay two, and the asymmetry between them is the rule: a county's posting may raise what this map shows, and a county's all-clear may never clean a measured exceedance.
scope_rules.verbatim: Minimum protective bacteriological standards for waters adjacent to public beaches and for public water-contact sports areas in ocean waters* are established in the California Code of Regulations, Title 17 (beginning at div. 1, ch. 5, § 7958 et seq.). When a public beach or public water-contact sports area fails to meet the standards, the California Department of Public Health or the local public health officer may post with warning signs or otherwise restrict use of the public beach or public water-contact sports area until the standards are met. The regulations impose more frequent monitoring and more stringent posting and closure requirements on certain high-use public beaches that are located adjacent to a storm drain that flows in the summer. The Title 17 bacteriological standards are not water quality objectives.

scope_rules.finding: The source itself says a geometric mean needs a statistically sufficient number of samples, 'generally not less than five samples distributed over a six-week period'. This is where the state's own 'Not enough data' tier comes from, and it is why sparse data yields no colour in this app: the state examined the same sparseness and withheld a status, and a split of 'Use caution' into two is not licence to speak where the state stayed silent.
scope_rules.verbatim: Only the GM* value shall be applied based on a statistically sufficient number of samples, which is generally not less than five samples distributed over a six-week period. However, if a statistically sufficient number of samples is not available to calculate the GM*, then attainment of the water quality objective shall be determined based only on the SSM* or STV*.

scope_rules.finding: The Bacteria Provisions state the same five-samples-over-six-weeks rule for waters outside the Ocean Plan's reach, so the sparse-data silence is not an ocean-only convention.

scope_rules.finding: AB 411 is a MONITORING AND POSTING mandate on local health officers for beaches over 50,000 annual visitors adjacent to a dry-weather storm drain — not a source of water quality objectives. Measured against the state's own Beach Detail resource, 188 of the 427 beaches this app plots are coded AB411Beach 'No', including Zuma, Santa Monica, Venice, Hermosa, Dockweiler and Avalon. Any claim that 'AB 411 governs' this app's readings is therefore wrong twice: wrong about the instrument, and inapplicable to 44 percent of the beaches.
scope_rules.verbatim: An AB411 beach is a California beach that is monitored under the regulations of the 1997 State Assembly Bill 411, which requires weekly bacterial testing from April 1st through October 31st of beaches visited by more than 50,000 people annually and located adjacent to a storm drain that flows in the dry weather for total coliform, fecal coliform, and enterococci bacteria. The law mandates that local health officials post warning signs and provide public information via a hotline when bacterial standards are exceeded to protect public health.

scope_rules.finding: The unit filter is the state's own line, not this app's: culture results are reported in CFU/100 mL or MPN/100 mL, and ddPCR results in copies/100 mL are 'presented separately'. The objectives above are stated in cfu/100 mL, so only culture units may be compared against them. Measured in the dataset, enterococcus against enterococcus: copies/100 mL results average about 61,600 while CFU/100 mL results average about 1,070 — banding molecular counts against a culture threshold reads every one of them as a catastrophic exceedance.

absent.what: The single-sample bacteria numbers a county health officer actually posts on, at California Code of Regulations title 17, division 1, chapter 5, section 7958 et seq.
absent.why_absent: No source this pipeline is permitted to fetch publishes them. California's regulations are published by a commercial host whose /robots.txt does not resolve (it 302-redirects to a site list), and leginfo.legislature.ca.gov serves 'Disallow: /'. The Ocean Plan cites the section but does not restate its numbers. Manual lane, and an owner sign-off item.
absent.consequence: The app cannot say what a county would post at, and must not present its own reading as a posting or its absence as an all-clear.

absent.what: A geometric-mean standard for ddPCR (copies/100 mL) enterococci.
absent.why_absent: None is published. The San Diego Water Board states plainly that it 'does not currently have a water-quality objective for Enterococcus ddPCR results'; the CDPH-derived 1,413 copies/100 mL is a SINGLE-SAMPLE advisory threshold and nothing more.
absent.consequence: ddPCR results can never produce a geometric-mean reading, only at most a single-sample one, and only in San Diego County.

absent.what: The published meaning of each ResultQualCode the state's bacteria results carry — the CEDEN ResQualLookUpList the dataset's own data dictionary refers the reader to.
absent.why_absent: The dictionary defines only '=' in its own words ('the recorded result is the actual result') and links the rest to ceden.org, which is not an allowlisted host for this pipeline. So this app holds no published definition of 'P' or 'DNQ'. Manual lane, and an owner sign-off item.
absent.consequence: The comparability of each code is THIS APP'S READING and is labelled as one. The inequality codes are read from their symbols; 'P' and 'DNQ' have no symbol to read, are not compared, and are not described. Measured 2026-09-04, calling a 'P' row presence-only was wrong on the data's own terms: all 400 such rows published since 2026-05-01 carry a positive numeric result and every one is carried into the state's own published six-week geometric mean, so this app is silent at stations where the state's own numbers yield a status.

absent.what: Any STATEWIDE live feed of beach closures or sewage spills.
absent.why_absent: There is no statewide one. The state's advisory/closure resource is published monthly and months in arrears, and the Safe to Swim map's host (mywaterquality.ca.gov) serves 'Disallow: /' to every agent but Googlebot, so it stays a link-out. NARROWED 2026-09-17 (R35): where a NAMED county publishes its own postings through a public data service this app reads, that county's posting IS shown — quoted in the county's own words, attributed to the county by name, and carried with the time this app read it. That covers the counties named in the app's own county list and no others; every county this app does not read is carried as absent, with the reason stated and the county's own hotline and page offered instead. A county's posting never replaces the tier computed from the state's samples, and a county's all-clear never cleans a measured exceedance.
absent.consequence: The app must SAY that no closure feed exists for the beaches where it reads none, and must never let its own silence stand for 'no closures' — which is the one thing this data can never support. Where a named county's own posting IS read, the app names the county, quotes it, and says when it read it; where it is not, the app says that too, and hands the reader the county's own hotline and page.

data_vocabularies.unit_filter_note: The objectives are stated in cfu/100 mL and the state presents molecular (copies/100 mL) results separately from culture results. Only culture units may be banded against an objective. This filter is NOT optional: it is the difference between reading a ddPCR count of tens of thousands as a catastrophic exceedance and not comparing it at all.
data_vocabularies.qualifier_note: A right-censored result ('>' or '>=') has no upper bound — an enterococcus result of '>20' could truly be 2,000 — so it is compared at its reported floor, where it can confirm an exceedance but can never support a clean reading. Left-censored results ('<', '<=', 'ND') are below their detection limit and are comparable as a maximum. 'P' and 'DNQ' are marked undefined_by_source: this app holds no published definition of them and does not compare them.
data_vocabularies.qualifier_comparability_note: The comparability column is THIS APP'S READING of each code, not the source's definition of it. The dataset's own data dictionary defines only '=' and refers the rest to a CEDEN lookup list this pipeline may not fetch (see the absence 'result_qualifier_code_definitions'). The inequality codes are read from their symbols. 'P' and 'DNQ' are not: measured 2026-09-04, all 400 'P' rows published since 2026-05-01 carry a positive numeric result between 10 and 9,208 and every one is carried into the state's own published six-week geometric mean, so describing them as presence-only with no number was a claim the data contradicts. They are not compared, and they are not characterised.
data_vocabularies.data_quality_note: The state's own quality flags. 'Reject Data' is not among them and never was. 'Spatial accuracy unknown' means the STATION'S COORDINATES are unreliable, which is a positional caveat, not a result caveat, and must be handled rather than passed through. The word 'verified' is unavailable to this app while the state flags its own data unknown.

data_vocabularies.published_geometric_mean_caveat: The state publishes its own 6-week geometric mean and sample count per row. Measured in the snapshot, right-censored results ('>' and '>=') are carried into that mean with 'No substitution' — at their reported floor. So where a window contains a right-censored sample the published geometric mean is a LOWER BOUND, and a mean that passes cannot be reported as clean.
